title: Run equilibrium calculations for all five conditions
action: Using a chemical equilibrium solver that performs Gibbs free energy minimization (Cantera or NASA CEA), compute the equilibrium gas-phase composition for the following five cases: (1) Moist air (77.45% N2, 20.59% O2, 2.00% H2O by mole) + 0.0305 g K2CO3 per liter of cold air, at T=1900 K, P=1 atm. (2) Same moist air + 0.04305 g Na2CO3 per liter, T=1900 K, P=1 atm. (3) Same moist air + 0.0305 g K2CO3 per liter, T=1700 K, P=1 atm. (4) Same moist air + 0.04305 g Na2CO3 per liter, T=1700 K, P=1 atm. (5) Stoichiometric propane-air mixture (C3H8 + 5 O2 + 18.80 N2) + 0.0305 g K2CO3 per liter of air volume, T=1900 K, P=1 atm. Convert the mass per liter of additive to moles using the ideal gas law at 298 K and 1 atm (1 liter of cold gas contains 0.04087 mol total gas) and the appropriate molar masses (K2CO3: 138.205 g/mol, Na2CO3: 105.988 g/mol). Save the full equilibrium mole fractions for all species (as percentages of the total mixture) in a structured file.
description: Generates the raw equilibrium compositions that are the foundation for the subsequent scored steps. Not directly scored.

title: Generate enthalpy-temperature curves
action: Using the same chemical equilibrium solver, compute the final temperature of the pure moist air mixture and the two additive-containing mixtures (moist air + K2CO3, moist air + Na2CO3) for a range of added enthalpy values. Use the initial compositions defined in Step 0 (the 1900 K cases) and perform a series of equilibrium calculations at fixed enthalpy (or at fixed temperature with subsequent enthalpy evaluation) to build temperature vs added enthalpy curves covering approximately 1500–2100 K. Save the resulting data (enthalpy, temperature) for each mixture in a file named `enthalpy_curves.json`.
description: Generates the enthalpy-temperature relations needed to extract the temperature reductions at the specified enthalpy addition.

title: Extract 1900 K moist-air mole fractions
action: From the equilibrium results produced in step_0, extract the mole percentages for the alkali species in the two 1900 K moist-air cases: for the K2CO3 case, KOH, K, KO; for the Na2CO3 case, NaOH, Na, NaO. Write a CSV file with columns: Case (either 'K2CO3' or 'Na2CO3'), Species (species name, one of KOH, K, KO, NaOH, Na, NaO), MolePercent (float, the mole percentage of that species in the total equilibrium mixture).
description: Mole fractions of the key alkali species at 1900 K, used to verify the tabulated equilibrium speciation.
output_schema: Case (string, one of 'K2CO3','Na2CO3'), Species (string, species name), MolePercent (float between 0 and 100).

title: Compute hydroxide percentages and temperature reductions for all conditions
action: Using the equilibrium compositions from step_0, compute the molar percentage of alkali present as gaseous hydroxide for each of the five conditions. For potassium cases: HydroxidePercent = 100 * KOH_mole_percent / (KOH_mole_percent + K_mole_percent + KO_mole_percent). For sodium cases: HydroxidePercent = 100 * NaOH_mole_percent / (NaOH_mole_percent + Na_mole_percent + NaO_mole_percent). Additionally, using the enthalpy-temperature curves from step_0b, determine the enthalpy addition H0 that brings pure moist air to approximately 1800 K. For the same H0, read the temperatures of the K2CO3 and Na2CO3 mixtures; compute the temperature reductions as (1800 K − mixture_temperature) for each. Write a CSV file with columns: Case, Temperature_K, HydroxidePercent, BaselineTemperature_K, TemperatureReduction_K. For the five hydroxide percentage rows, fill Temperature_K and HydroxidePercent as above. For the two 1900 K moist-air rows (K2CO3 and Na2CO3), set BaselineTemperature_K=1800 and TemperatureReduction_K to the computed reductions (in Kelvin). For all other rows, set BaselineTemperature_K=1800 and TemperatureReduction_K=0 or NaN (they will be ignored by the verifier).
description: Molar percentage of alkali present as gaseous hydroxide for all five conditions, plus the temperature reductions for the two main moist-air cases at 1900 K. The hydroxide percentages are the main speciation claim; the reductions add the paper's headline temperature diminution.
